title: What happened in AI — Jun 7, 2026
intro: The practical edges of AI, not new frontier models, held the spotlight on a quiet Sunday. The day's most-discussed item wasn't an announcement at all but a community gut-check: an Ask HN thread polling what people actually reach for in AI coding today — which clients and harnesses, which providers, which local setups — a useful snapshot of a fast-churning tooling landscape.

On the hardware and infrastructure side, NVIDIA carried its COMPUTEX momentum into Korea, promoting the RTX Spark superchip for the era of personal AI agents, while AWS's open-source ExtendDB gave developers a DynamoDB-compatible API atop pluggable storage backends, starting with PostgreSQL.
highlights: An Ask HN thread took the community's pulse on which AI coding tools, harnesses, and providers people actually use day to day.
NVIDIA pushed its RTX Spark superchip — pitched for the era of personal AI agents — at Korea's PC Bangs following its COMPUTEX debut.
AWS open-sourced ExtendDB, a DynamoDB-compatible adapter with pluggable storage backends, beginning with PostgreSQL.
